title: Casper and the Sigil
premise: Dominic Fairweather, cartographer and ledger-keeper for the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers his own name in a century-old book of prophecies dated tonight. The prophecy names him the unmaker of a king — but the king is already dead, replaced by a sigil-bound thing that feeds on the city's memory. To fulfill or refuse the prophecy, Dominic must gather a ragged found family of guild misfits, unbind the sigil before it consumes the realm's past entirely, and learn that belonging is something you build, not something you're granted. In the end he breaks the sigil at the cost of the guild's ledgers, erasing himself from every map and record — only to be rewritten into existence by the people who choose to remember him.
about_author: Casper Sandoval is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging maps of places that no longer exist. They write fantasy about people who find each other in the margins of official histories.

chapters.title: The Date That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. While balancing the guild's ledgers, Dominic finds tonight's date inscribed in a sealed prophetic text, followed by his own name and the words 'the unbinding.' Before he can alert anyone, the ink pulls him through the page into the royal city of Vaelmoor, where bells toll for a king who died weeks ago. Emotional beat: disorientation sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: A Crown of Borrowed Light
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Navigating Vaelmoor's streets, Dominic witnesses the 'king' preside over a festival where citizens cheer with hollow eyes, their memories visibly dimming. A pickpocket named Wren saves him from a sigil-warden patrol and recognizes him from her grandmother's stories. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into horror, then the first spark of alliance.

chapters.title: The Guild of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren leads Dominic through hidden ways to the guild's sanctuary: a tinkerer who repairs broken promises, a disgraced royal historian, and an ex-sigil-warden named Brannoc who knows how the binding works. They confirm the prophecy is real and that Dominic is its instrument. Emotional beat: wary strangers becoming, tentatively, a team.

chapters.title: What the Sigil Eats
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Brannoc explains the sigil was meant to preserve the dying king but instead devours memory to sustain itself; the city forgets its dead, its debts, its wrongs. Justice itself is dissolving. The guild realizes they must reach the crown vault within nine days, when the last recorded memories burn away. Emotional beat: grief for what's being erased, resolve kindling.

chapters.title: The Historian's Confession
chapters.summary: Historian Maren's POV. Maren reveals she helped forge the records that let the sigil take the throne, believing she was preserving stability. Her guilt gives them the vault's true entrance — through the Hall of Forgotten Names. Meanwhile warden patrols close in, tipped by someone inside the guild. Emotional beat: shame transformed into purpose.

chapters.title: The Traitor in the Margins
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The traitor is revealed as Tallow, the promise-tinkerer, whose own forgotten daughter is held in the sigil's keeping. He betrays their route to buy her back. Dominic confronts him not with anger but with the ledger itself, showing Tallow his daughter's name still written there. Emotional beat: heartbreak, and forgiveness offered without guarantee.

chapters.title: Nine Bells
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. With two days left, the guild makes its assault on the Hall of Forgotten Names while the city celebrates the Festival of Unending Reign. Wren, who has spent her life unseen, becomes visible in the worst way — captured by wardens and brought before the king-thing, which offers her everything she never had. Emotional beat: temptation at its most seductive.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing His Crown
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic trades himself for Wren, standing before the sigil-king, which shows him a vision of belonging: a world where everyone remembers him, loves him, keeps him. He nearly accepts. Then he sees the vision's seams — love that is manufactured is not love. He refuses, and the sigil marks him for unmaking. Emotional beat: the darkest hour, chosen freely.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. In the crown vault, the guild fights the wardens while Dominic reads the counter-prophecy aloud, unbinding the sigil line by line. It resists by offering the dead king's final memory: the truth that he chose this fate to save his people. Dominic honors the king by finishing the work anyway. The sigil shatters; the ledgers burn as payment. Emotional beat: climax — sacrifice, grief, and release.

chapters.title: Written By Those Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The city wakes remembering its dead and its debts; justice returns as trials, reparations, reckonings. But Dominic is fading, unwritten from every record. One by one, Wren, Brannoc, Maren, even Tallow speak his name into new pages they write themselves, rebuilding him from testimony rather than ink. He remains — not because a book said so, but because they do. Emotional beat: belonging earned, home made.
